learn.title: Letters on both sides
learn.body: Sometimes $x$ appears on both sides, like $5x+2=3x+10$. The plan stays the same: do the same thing to both sides. First gather all the $x$ terms on one side.

learn.title: Solve $5x+2=3x+10$
learn.body: Move the $x$ terms together, then solve as before.

learn.title: Solve $7x-3=2x+12$
learn.body: Subtract the smaller $x$ term so the coefficient stays positive.
You may gather the $x$ terms on either side. Choosing the side with the bigger coefficient avoids negative numbers, but both choices give the same answer.

learn.title: When things cancel
learn.body: Look at $2x+1=2x+5$. Subtracting $2x$ gives $1=5$, which is never true, so there is no solution. If you get something always true, like $3=3$, every number is a solution.

questions.prompt: To solve $5x+2=3x+10$, first subtract \_\_ from both sides.
questions.explanation: Subtracting $3x$ moves every $x$ to the left side and leaves $2x+2=10$.

questions.prompt: Solve $3x+4=x+10$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: First gather the $x$ terms on one side, then the plain numbers on the other, then divide.
Add $x$ to both sides: $10=4x+2$. Subtract 2: $8=4x$, so $x=2$. Check: $8=8$.
Subtract $2x$ and 3 from both sides: $4x=0$, so $x=0$. A solution of zero is still a solution.
Subtract $3x$ from both sides and you get $5=9$, which is false for every $x$. So there is no solution.
